title: Only what he strives for
hook: a person has only what he strives for, and his striving will be seen (53:39–40)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Muntaha, the farthest limit, marked by a lote tree. Your line was the farthest tree.

Day six hundred. However those mornings came, with full attention, half-asleep, or pressing play just to keep the streak alive, they were somebody's effort. A milestone invites a tally: days, streaks, minutes. Surah An-Najm keeps a different kind. It's about what a person ends up holding at the end: not what they hoped for, not what they inherited, not what someone said about them. What they actually strove for, and nothing else.

Verses thirty-nine and forty, in Pickthall's translation: "And that man hath only that for which he maketh effort, And that his effort will be seen." The word is sa'y: striving, effort, going toward something on purpose. If you've followed the pilgrimage, you've met it. The sa'y is the walk, seven times, between the hills of Safa and Marwah, remembering Hajar running between them searching for water for her baby, Isma'il. Effort as a body moving toward what it needs. The verse sits in a passage the surah says was in the scrolls of Musa and of Ibrahim: no soul carries another's burden, and a person has only what they strive for. Two promises come out of it. Nobody can take your effort from you, or be credited with it in your place. And it will be seen, not necessarily by people. Seen. Scholars raise an honest question here. What about charity given for the dead, or prayers for a parent who's gone? Hadith in Bukhari and Muslim say such things do reach the dead. Scholars reconcile it in different ways. Some say a righteous child is part of the parent's own striving: a hadith in Muslim names a good child who prays for you among the three things that continue after death. Others say the verse sets the rule of justice, and Allah's generosity can add to it. Either way, in the verse's words, a person's effort is theirs, and it will be seen.
screen: `SA'Y: EFFORT TOWARD A NEED.` · `HAJAR, BETWEEN SAFA AND MARWAH.` · `YOURS, AND IT WILL BE SEEN.` · `WHAT REACHES THE DEAD? SCHOLARS WEIGH IT.`

segments.voice: Picture Hajar's walk: back and forth between two hills, looking, not giving up. Then bring to mind one thing that deserves your real effort, a hard conversation, a task you keep postponing, a person who needs you, and see yourself doing it fully, not halfway. If you pray, ask for strength in it.
Sa'y: in 53:39, a person has only their effort, and in 53:40, that effort will be seen. Today's word.
Your line: only what you strive for. In the verse's words, it will be seen. Six hundred days, and counting.

chat.says: What does An-Najm mean by 'only what he strives for'?
options: Your effort is yours; no one else is credited with it, and it will be seen.
Only results count; effort that falls short isn't recorded at all.
Only effort made on pilgrimage, like the walk at Safa, really counts.
chat.meaning: 53:39–40: a person has only what they strive for, and their effort will be seen. No soul carries another's burden.
